label: v fed back as input on the final copy step of short (L<=4) sequences
explanation: Token-specific copy-phase feature: fires only when the input is v during the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phase, never on any other input token, never on the first occurrence of v). The strongest and most precise activations (dev precision 0.98, about 77% of activation mass) are at the last copy step of short sequences, mainly L=4 at t=7 (e.g. a l v v <DEL> a l [v]), plus L=3 at t=5. A weaker tail fires on v inputs one step before the end (to_go=1) or at the end of L=5 sequences (about 30% of such steps, low magnitude), and it is almost silent for L>=6. Magnitude is largest at L=4 / to_go=0 and drops off for longer sequences and earlier copy positions. Broader v-in-copy-phase predicates reach full recall but low precision (0.06).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: v, -, e, m, u, q; least: b, 3, k, d) and the token being output (most: v, m, d, k, u, e; least: f, l, g, -); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=4 & t=7, recall_idx=4.
